canonical_claim: For a set X in real affine n-space definable in an o-minimal expansion of the real field and every real epsilon > 0, there is a positive constant c such that, for every height threshold T >= 1, the number of rational points of affine height at most T in X outside the algebraic part of X is at most c * T^epsilon.
domain_and_universes: L : FirstOrder.Language.{0,0}; L.Structure Real; n : Nat; X : Set (Fin n -> Real); epsilon c : Real; T : Nat; root in Prop.
quantifiers: o-minimal expansion of the real field
positive constant c depending on X and epsilon
hypotheses: the ambient structure is an o-minimal expansion of the real field
X is definable in that structure
conclusion: The bounded-height rational points in X minus its algebraic part form a finite set whose cardinality is at most c * T^epsilon.

degenerate_cases: T=0 and epsilon<=0 are excluded. n=0, empty X, and zero-dimensional X are admitted; pointHeight on Q^0 is proved zero. The affine height bound is nonstrict and T is natural with T>=1.
